polity.canonical_name_en: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata

activity.notes: José de San Martín entered the service of the Río de la Plata revolutionary government in 1812, when the Triumvirate recognized his rank and appointed him to organize and command the Mounted Grenadiers. He subsequently commanded the Army of the North, governed Cuyo, and built the Army of the Andes under the authority of the United Provinces. In 1820 the central Directorial government collapsed; the Act of Rancagua preserved his independent emancipation command after that institutional break. ATLAS therefore uses 1812-1820 as his primary United Provinces service Activity. His later office as Protector of Peru in 1821-1822 is a distinct polity and office and is not merged into this Activity.

sources.title: Cronología Sanmartiniana — Instituto Nacional Sanmartiniano
sources.citation_text: The Instituto Nacional Sanmartiniano chronology records San Martín's return to Buenos Aires and his March 1812 appointment to organize the Mounted Grenadiers, later commands, and the 1820 institutional rupture surrounding the Act of Rancagua.

sources.title: 17 de agosto: Paso a la Inmortalidad del General José de San Martín — Argentina.gob.ar
sources.citation_text: Argentina's official government biography describes San Martín's governorship of Cuyo, the approval of his continental plan by the United Provinces government, and formation of the Army of the Andes.

sources.title: Abril: un mes decisivo en la vida del General José de San Martín y en el recuerdo de su legado — Instituto Nacional Sanmartiniano
sources.citation_text: The Instituto Nacional Sanmartiniano explains the 1820 Act of Rancagua and the continuation of San Martín's emancipation command after the expiration of the central United Provinces authorities.
